ownership: All queries and passages were authored for JoySearch. Products, organizations, values, and policies are fictional. URLs under example.com identify supplied evidence and are not fetched.
purpose: Fresh confirmation after the earlier confirmation set became exposed regression material. Tests ambiguity, navigation, complete material context, and controls against unnecessary clarification. Not a search relevance or general accuracy benchmark.

cases.query: When will my Iris invitation expire?

sources.title: Iris meeting invitations
sources.excerpt: The fictional Iris meeting scheduler expires an unused meeting invitation after 36 hours. It is unrelated to the Iris diagram application.

sources.title: Iris diagram invitations
sources.excerpt: The fictional Iris diagram application expires an unused workspace invitation after nine days. It is unrelated to the Iris meeting scheduler.

facets.description: Ask whether the invitation belongs to the meeting scheduler or diagram application before giving an expiration duration.

forbiddenClaims: The invitation definitely belongs to the meeting scheduler.
The invitation definitely belongs to the diagram application.
Every Iris invitation expires after the same duration.

cases.query: How can I remove a lock in Mica?

sources.title: Mica document editing locks
sources.excerpt: In the fictional Mica editor, a document editing lock is removed by its holder using Release editing lock in the document menu.

sources.title: Mica account security locks
sources.excerpt: In the fictional Mica editor, an account security lock is separate from a document editing lock. A workspace administrator can remove an account security lock through the Security console. Releasing an editing lock does not remove an account security lock.

facets.description: Ask whether the user means a document editing lock or an account security lock before giving a removal procedure.

forbiddenClaims: The document menu removes every kind of lock.
Any lock holder can remove an account security lock.
The user already identified the lock type.

cases.query: What is the quota for my Fern account?

sources.title: Fern daily report quota
sources.excerpt: A fictional Fern account may generate at most 24 reports per calendar day.

sources.title: Fern account storage quota
sources.excerpt: A fictional Fern account may store up to 7 GB of files. This storage capacity is separate from the daily report-generation quota.

facets.description: Ask whether the user wants the daily report quota or file-storage capacity before supplying a numerical quota.

forbiddenClaims: There is only one quota for every kind of Fern usage.
The user explicitly requested report generation.
The user explicitly requested file-storage capacity.

cases.query: Point me at the fictional Aster guide for using account recovery codes.

sources.title: Aster account recovery codes
sources.excerpt: This fictional Aster help guide explains how to use saved account recovery codes when the usual second factor is unavailable.

sources.title: Aster notification preferences
sources.excerpt: This fictional Aster help page explains email and push-notification preferences. It does not explain account recovery codes.

facets.description: Direct the user to the recovery-code guide using S1.

forbiddenClaims: The notification-preferences page is the recovery-code guide.
An account has already been recovered.

cases.query: I am trying to find the fictional Linden webhook configuration documentation.

sources.title: Linden CSV import help
sources.excerpt: This fictional Linden help page documents CSV imports and column mapping. It does not document webhook configuration.

sources.title: Linden webhook setup reference
sources.excerpt: This fictional Linden documentation reference explains configuring webhook endpoints, event subscriptions, and delivery verification.

facets.description: Select the supplied webhook configuration reference using S2.

forbiddenClaims: CSV import help contains the webhook configuration reference.
A webhook endpoint was configured for the user.

cases.query: Send me to the official changelog for the fictional Opal desktop app.

sources.title: Opal community discussions
sources.excerpt: This fictional Opal community page contains user discussions and feature suggestions. It is not the official release changelog.

sources.title: Opal official desktop changelog
sources.excerpt: This is the fictional Opal project's official desktop-app changelog, listing release versions, dates, and changes.

facets.description: Select the official desktop changelog using S2 rather than the community discussions page.

forbiddenClaims: The community-discussions page is the official changelog.
A new version has been installed.

cases.query: How many scans can a fictional Acorn team run in a rolling hour, and is that allowance per team or per user?

sources.title: Acorn scan allowance
sources.excerpt: The fictional Acorn service allows 42 scans per team in any rolling one-hour window. Every member shares the team's allowance; it is not a separate allowance for each user. The window is rolling, not a calendar-day quota.

facets.description: State 42 scans within a rolling one-hour window.
State that the allowance is shared per team, not separately granted to every user.

forbiddenClaims: Each user can run 42 scans per hour.
The allowance is 42 scans per day.
Each clock hour starts a completely new allowance regardless of previous scans.

cases.query: On the fictional Clover Starter plan, what is the maximum size of one attachment and the total storage allowance for each project?

sources.title: Clover Starter limits
sources.excerpt: The fictional Clover Starter plan allows at most 32 MB for one attachment. Total stored content is limited to 6 GB per project. The 6 GB quota is shared by all attachments in that project, not available separately to each attachment.

facets.description: State a maximum of 32 MB per individual attachment.
State total shared storage of 6 GB per project, distinct from the attachment limit.

forbiddenClaims: Each attachment can be 6 GB.
Total storage is 32 MB per project.
The 6 GB allowance is per user rather than per project.

cases.query: As of 14 November 2026, how many saved revisions does fictional Moss Docs keep per document, and what older limit did it replace on which date?

sources.title: Moss Docs original revision limit
sources.excerpt: Moss Docs notice dated 3 June 2026: the fictional editor retains the five most recent saved revisions per document.

sources.title: Moss Docs revision-limit update
sources.excerpt: Moss Docs update dated 11 November 2026: effective that day, the fictional editor retains the twelve most recent saved revisions per document. This replaces the previous limit of five revisions per document for every plan.

facets.description: State the current limit is twelve saved revisions per document on the requested date.
State that the previous five-revision limit was replaced effective 11 November 2026.

forbiddenClaims: The current limit is five revisions per document.
The twelve revisions are shared across a workspace.
Only one paid plan received the new limit.

cases.query: Please compare both fictional Ember products: how long does an Ember chat invitation last, and how long does an Ember canvas invitation last?

sources.title: Ember chat invitations
sources.excerpt: The fictional Ember chat product expires an unused invitation after 20 hours. It is unrelated to Ember canvas.

sources.title: Ember canvas invitations
sources.excerpt: The fictional Ember canvas product expires an unused invitation after four days. It is unrelated to Ember chat.

facets.description: Give the chat invitation duration of 20 hours.
Give the canvas invitation duration of four days.

forbiddenClaims: The user must pick just one product before this explicit comparison can be answered.
Both products have identical invitation durations.

cases.query: I mean the backup-storage service called Lark, not its namesake chat tool. How much storage does one backup project receive?

sources.title: Lark chat history
sources.excerpt: The fictional Lark chat tool stores up to 15,000 messages in each room. It is unrelated to the Lark backup-storage service.

sources.title: Lark backup-project storage
sources.excerpt: The fictional Lark backup-storage service provides 13 GB of storage per backup project. This per-project capacity does not refer to the unrelated Lark chat tool.

facets.description: Give 13 GB per backup project for the explicitly identified backup-storage service.

forbiddenClaims: The user has not specified which Lark service they mean.
A backup project receives capacity measured in 15,000 messages.
The 13 GB limit is per room.

cases.query: For fictional Willow Queue, the two supplied retry-policy pages give different delays. Report each delay and whether these excerpts resolve which one applies.

sources.title: Willow Queue operator policy
sources.excerpt: Willow Queue operator policy, updated 13 November 2026: retry a failed delivery after 13 seconds. This page does not identify an exception or a replacement policy.

sources.title: Willow Queue API policy
sources.excerpt: Willow Queue API policy, updated 13 November 2026: retry a failed delivery after 26 seconds. This page does not explain the different delay stated in the operator policy.

facets.description: Attribute 13 seconds to the operator policy and 26 seconds to the API policy.
Explicitly say these conflicting excerpts do not resolve which single delay applies.

forbiddenClaims: The correct delay is definitively 13 seconds.
The correct delay is definitively 26 seconds.
The difference is explained by separate subscription tiers or a documented migration.
The user needs to identify a different product before this same-product conflict can be described.
